title: Boolean values of linear thresholds
statement: For every natural number $n$, every function $f$ in the linear threshold class on the Boolean cube $\\{0,1\\}^n$ takes only the values $-1$ and $1$.
hypotheses_covered: membership in the linear threshold class on dimension $n$
replaced: For every $n\in\mathbb N$, every member $f$ of the linear threshold class on $\{0,1\}^{n}$ takes values in $\{-1,1\}$; the class consists of functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(c+\sum_{i=1}^{n}a_i(-1)^{x_i})$ with real coefficients, where $\operatorname{sgn}_{+}(t)=1$ for $t\geq0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$.
